description:
The UI's branch-state classifier and ARCH §7.1 disagree on what
constitutes `Stopped` for an unmerged branch.

ARCH §7.1 (line 386):
  > `stopped`: branch is unmerged, the latest step's
  > `response.json` is closed, and its last JSONL event is
  > **not** `message_stop`

Current UI implementation
(`crates/lernie-ui-egui/src/git_tree/state.rs::has_terminal_event`):
treats both `message_stop` AND `error` as terminal events, returning
`BranchState::Stopped` when the last completed line is either.

Why the spec is right (and the UI is wrong):
- For a subagent step that emitted `message_stop`, the harness
  still has terminal compaction + merge-back to do (§2.3 step 5,
  §2.6, §2.7). The chain is mid-progress, not stopped.
- For a root conversation between steps, the latest step ends in
  `message_stop` and the next step has not yet been written. The
  branch is in_flight, not stopped — the UI flickers "stopped"
  during normal multi-step exchanges.
- The post-bl-c9ec await built-in already follows ARCH §7.1: it
  treats `message_stop` as InFlight and uses the §3.5 fd-open
  observation (via `PgidFinder` /proc-fd scan) to disambiguate
  mid-stream from kill-mid-stream. The UI is the last consumer
  still on the pre-spec interpretation.

Scope:
- Update `has_terminal_event` (or replace it) so `message_stop`
  alone does NOT classify as `Stopped`. The spec-correct rule is:
  unmerged AND fd-closed AND last completed line is not
  `message_stop`. `error` remains a Stopped signal regardless of
  fd state.
- The fd-closed check needs a signal the UI doesn't currently
  track. Options (pick on merit):
  1. inotify CLOSE_WRITE via the existing `notify`-based
     `fs_watcher` (matches ARCH §3.5 line 384 — "Completion
     signal: writer closes the fd; inotify `IN_CLOSE_WRITE` marks
     the response complete"). The watcher is already running; this
     is a classifier-side change to consume CLOSE_WRITE events.
  2. /proc fd-scan via the same `PgidFinder` await uses. Cross-
     crate, so requires plumbing or a shared crate.
  Option 1 is the canonical UI approach per the spec.
- Tests: extend `state.rs::tests` so `message_stop`-without-close
  classifies as `InFlight`, `message_stop`-with-close classifies
  as `Stopped`, and the existing `error` cases still work.

Out of scope:
- Re-architecting the renderer; the change is local to the
  classifier and its watcher input.
- The harness side — `await` (post bl-c9ec) and `lernie stop`
  already match the spec.
title: UI classifier: message_stop is not a Stopped signal (ARCH §7.1 misalignment)
